newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES END MARGINALLY WEAKER IN SLOW TRADING.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES END MARGINALLY WEAKER IN SLOW TRADING.

text.p: The Greek stockmarket settled 0.09 percent lower in lethargic trading after losing its enthusiasm for OTE telecom which had earlier produced a general mood of optimism, traders said.
"The market suffers from flagging interest as we enter the vacation season, as evidenced by today's meagre trading volume," said George Ventouratos, fund manager at Aspis mutual funds.
"Today's session was enlivened by the comeback of Titan Cement and OTE which had been depressed in the previous days," he added.
Rates on the interbank market, pushed higher last week by a brief episode of drachma weakness, were easing across the curve.
The one-month Athibor, Greece's reference interbank rate, eased to 12.58 percent from Friday's 12.73 percent.

"Investors remain cautious over short-term interest rates but the overall level of rates should resume its downward course from September onwards," Ventouratos said. "In the meantime, stocks will be mainly moved by interim results."
OTE telecom outperformed the market gaining 70 drachmas to 6,215 and rebounding from recent weakness.
"OTE's stock appears very attractive at current price levels and should yield good return in the medium-term," said Ventouratos.
A report in the 'Sunday Eleftherotypia' newspaper suggested that the government was contemplating the introduction of a capital gains tax on equities.
Currently, there is no taxation on gains from Greek stocks.
"The chance of the introduction of a capital gains tax in the near future appears very remote," said a floor trader. "It was not at the back of anybody's mind during today's trading."
The Athens general index settled a net 0.09 percent or 1.40 points lower at 1,535.69 from Friday's 1,537.09 close, having fluctuated between 1,528 and 1,547 points.
Industrials edged up 0.03 percent and banks slipped 0.43 percent.
Turnover was poor, reaching 8.8 billion drachmas on volume of 2.8 million shares, including a put-through order for 50,000 shares of Alpha Leasing , executed at 7,270/7,300 drachmas.
Decliners led advancers 112 to 77 with 28 shares unchanged on 217 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.5-$10.8. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,115-1,145 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,042-1,102 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock firmed 70 drachmas to 6,215.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 590.89-628.61 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $66.30-$69.02. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,076-3,291 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $10.79 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 208-239 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
